detailed_description:
LOCATION MAP: The crossroads of two muddy roads in open winter pasture. THE TREE, a single ancient leafless oak, stands at the right-hand front corner of the crossroads; its thick LOW LIMB runs almost horizontally out over the verge toward the centre of the crossroads. A rough LADDER leans against the trunk on the road side. The low HITCHING POST stands in the same verge a few paces from the trunk. At the foot of the tree, among the huge knuckled ROOTS, the earth is black, soft and bare. THE BACK ROAD enters at the far left round a BEND hidden by a bare thorn HEDGE; THE ROAD AHEAD leaves to the right, straight, long and open; THE OPPOSITE ROAD comes down toward us from a low bare HILL far behind. Nothing else stands in the open fields. Camera side: the camera stands on the back-road side of the crossroads, looking toward the tree, which stays at frame-right. The 180° line is the line between the bend in the hedge and the tree; the camera stays on its side of that line.

ACTION TIMING:
[0.00s–5.00s] [[ACTION]]
Nobody speaks in this shot.
PEOPLE: RENAUD: a gaunt, underfed man around forty with hollow cheeks and temples, a long face with the skin drawn tight over the bones and greyish from lack of sleep, weather-beaten, dark shadowed eyes that do not settle on anything, a thin dark beard grown out untrimmed and uneven, cracked lips, matted dark hair roughly cut; a mail coif pushed back off his head onto his shoulders, over a plain dark brown gambeson with no ornament, a sword on a belt cinched two holes tighter than its old mark, no hat; he stands slightly apart from anyone else in frame. || AYMER: a heavy-set man in his mid-forties with a broad weathered face, a short grey-streaked beard, deep lines from nose to mouth, small tired grey eyes under heavy brows, a nose broken once and badly set; greying brown hair cut in the thirteenth-century bowl style, a straight sparse fringe level across the forehead, covering the top half of the ears, thinning on top, unwashed and pressed flat from the helmet; he wears a rusted mail hauberk over a dirty quilted gambeson, a plain leather belt with a sword in a worn scabbard, no surcoat, no heraldry; he stands with his weight off his right hip.
CHARACTER ACTING: RENAUD turns his thin horse across the first stranger's path and takes the cut for it without a sound. After the burial he stands alone before the figure on the low limb and looks up at it for a long time, the only one who does; his jaw works once. He turns only when Aymer's hand lands on his shoulder. He rides out last on one of the strangers' horses, leading his own wounded horse gently by the halter, and does not look back.
AYMER dismounts badly, weight off the right hip, and goes to meet the second stranger on foot. He cuts to disarm, sees the man pass the sword to his left hand without a sound, and keeps working. After the fight he crouches in two stages to take the sword from the seated man, not sure he is dead, checking one beat longer than a soldier needs. He drags and tips the bodies without ceremony, then lays a flat hand on Renaud's shoulder to move him on.
PHYSICS: Real weight: feet sink into soft mud and crack frozen ruts, breath steams, cloth and gear move with the body; any animal already in the first frame shifts its weight and blows.
LIGHTING: Early winter afternoon under a low, even overcast sky: flat, cold grey light with no sun and no hard shadows, frost in the wheel ruts, breath visible; the light falls slowly as the scene goes on.
STYLE: Photorealistic live-action medieval drama, thirteenth century, grounded and naturalistic, in open northern European farmland; muted desaturated palette, aged mud-stained costumes, no fantasy.
QUALITY: Photorealistic from frame zero; identities, costumes and animals consistent across the whole take; natural motion blur; no morphing.
